metadata.title: Fever guidance for adults and children

text:
Section 1: Fever basics. Fever is a common sign of infection or illness. A mild fever may improve with rest, fluids, and monitoring. Regularly assess temperature and symptoms, and avoid relying on a single reading alone when the person appears well.

Section 2: When to seek help. Seek urgent care if the person has trouble breathing, chest pain, confusion, severe dehydration, or a fever that is not improving. In children, a high fever with lethargy or poor feeding also needs medical review.

Section 3: Home care. Keep the person hydrated, rest, and monitor for worsening symptoms. Use a thermometer and note duration, severity, and warning signs before contacting a clinician.
